record.paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Let Σ be an alphabet and let w ∈ Σ∗ a p-free word. Then w is a factor of a maximal p-free word over Σ.

evidence.quote: Let Σ be an alphabet and let w ∈ Σ∗ a p-free word. Then w is a factor of a maximal p-free word over Σ.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and let $\Sigma^*$ denote the set of finite words over $\Sigma$. A pattern is a word $p$ over an alphabet of variables $V = \{x_1, x_2, \ldots\}$. A word $w \in \Sigma^*$ is said to contain an occurrence of $p$ if there exists a non-erasing morphism $h : V^* \to \Sigma^*$ such that $h(p)$ is a factor of $w$; otherwise, $w$ is called $p$-free. A $p$-free word $u \in \Sigma^*$ is called maximal (with respect to $p$ over $\Sigma$) if for every letter $a \in \Sigma$, neither $au$ nor $ua$ is $p$-free, i.e., $u$ cannot be extended on either side while remaining $p$-free.

Prove or disprove the following statement: for every finite alphabet $\Sigma$, every pattern $p$, and every $p$-free word $w \in \Sigma^*$, there exists a maximal $p$-free word $u \in \Sigma^*$ over $\Sigma$ such that $w$ is a factor of $u$.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a published resolution of this extension/maximality conjecture for $p$-free words. It is listed among open problems in combinatorics on words but no proof or counterexample was located in recent literature on pattern avoidance.

status_evidence.title: Pattern Avoidance and HDOL Words
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Cassaigne-type conjectures on words avoiding patterns; no resolution of the maximal-extension conjecture is given.
status_evidence.claim: Related conjectures on $p$-free words remain studied without a recorded resolution of the maximal-extension question.

status_evidence.title: Avoidability of palindrome patterns (Ochem)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on avoidable patterns over finite alphabets; does not address the extension-to-maximal claim.
status_evidence.claim: Recent pattern-avoidance literature does not report a proof or disproof of the conjecture.
